channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: From Wall Street to Main Street, how artificial intelligence is affecting the economy
item.description: Artificial intelligence is sending shock waves through the stock market, as investors try to predict how their big bets will pay off. Meanwhile some real businesses are putting AI to work, with mixed results.

item.title: Chief economist for Moody's Analytics on why Anthropic's IPO caused market volatility
item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Mark Zandi, chief economist for Moody's Analytics, about Anthropic's Wall Street debut and why it seems to have triggered recent market volatility.

item.title: Thanksgiving storms threaten travel on both coasts
item.description: Both coasts are going to be battered by Thanksgiving storms, just as millions travel to share the holiday with family and friends. Expect the weather to delay flights and make driving difficult.

item.title: K is for kindness, but families worry the world has less of it
item.description: A decade after first asking families about kindness, Sesame Workshop asked parents similar questions. They responded that their kids are getting kinder even as the wider world becomes less so.

item.title: Let's talk turkey: Here's how Thanksgiving meal costs have changed this year
item.description: Grocery costs have been on the rise, but food-price analysts say it's unclear if you'll spend more on the Thanksgiving meal this year. Some people are deciding not to host or are hosting fewer guests.
